tagline: Concentric waves with four shapes and four polarisations — pond drops, VHS rolls, neon grids
description: Wave distortion with a real physics backbone. Four wave shapes — Sine, Triangle, Square, and Sawtooth — produce everything from gentle water rings to hard digital glitches. Four polarisation modes — Radial (pond-drop circles), Horizontal, Vertical, and Diagonal — change where the wave energy propagates. A Decay slider attenuates the wave from center outward so inner rings are tightest and outer rings fade naturally. Phase shifts the entire wave cycle for animation-ready offset loops.

faq.q: What polarisation should I use for a classic water-drop effect?
faq.a: Radial. It propagates the wave as concentric rings from the center point — exactly how a drop hitting still water looks. Set Wavelength around 30 px and Amplitude around 8-12 px for a realistic scale.

faq.q: How do I get a VHS scan-line roll look?
faq.a: Set Polarisation to Vertical, Wave to Sawtooth, Amplitude high (40-60 px), Wavelength wide (80-120 px), and Decay near zero. This mimics the way VHS tracking errors bend horizontal scan lines.
Phase is designed for this — increment it from 0 to 360 across frames for a forward-flowing wave. Combined with a Square wave and Horizontal polarisation you get the classic neon-grid warp.
